item.description:
The first build of Crisper. Every other memory tool waits for you to go looking; this one asks a different question at save time — not where does this go? but when should this come back to me? — and answers it with a situation rather than a folder.

Capture, four ways

  • ⌃Space from anywhere opens the composer, over whatever you are working in. It never steals focus, and it remembers where you left it.
  • Drag onto the menu bar icon — files, a link, a selection of text. Up to eight at once, each classified on its own.
  • Talk to it. Voice notes are transcribed on this Mac and never leave it.
  • Drop it in the panel and drag more in while it is open.

It works out what you saved

Crisper proposes a kind, a title and a trigger while you type, using Apple's on-device model where your Mac supports it and a built-in classifier where it does not. The guess is shown before anything is written, and one tap corrects it. Nothing is saved until you press Drop.

It comes back on its own

Bind something to an app or a category and it surfaces when you get there — a font when you open Figma, a reference when you open the browser. The menu bar icon carries a count and nothing else: no banner, no sound, no window taking your place. Open it when you want it.

Good to know

  • Requires macOS 26 or later. On Apple silicon with Apple Intelligence enabled you get on-device classification; without it everything still works, with simpler guesses.
  • Everything lives on this Mac. No account, no sign-up, no server.
  • Crisper keeps itself up to date and will show you what changed before installing anything.
  • This is an alpha, and it is honest about being one — iCloud sync, semantic search and the feedback loop that learns from what you open are all still to come.
